description: Pre-specified rules for the v2 placebo-subtracted liability labels (P33.2). Written and committed before any extraction result was inspected. scripts/v2_liabilities.py reads this file and records its sha256 in truth/liabilities.json; changing a rule changes the hash.

term_matching.normalisation: Row label lowercased; footnote markers (*, dagger, double dagger, section sign, superscript letters/digits in <sup>), trailing colons and repeated whitespace removed. Text in parentheses is split off and kept as the row's 'includes' note.
term_matching.match: A row matches a liability when its normalised label (parenthetical removed) equals one of the liability's terms, or when the label is a compound joined by '/', ',' or ' or ' and any component equals a term. Substring matching is not used: 'tardive dyskinesia' must not match 'dyskinesia', 'hypotension' must not match 'orthostatic hypotension'.
term_matching.grouped_terms: A row is a grouped term when its label is one of the liability's grouped_terms, or carries a parenthetical 'includes ...' note, or is a compound containing two or more of the liability's terms. When a placebo-controlled table has a grouped row for a liability, that row is used alone. Otherwise the liability value per arm is the MAX over its matched single-term rows, never the sum (the same patient can report several terms, so summing double-counts).

excluded.tremor: Non-specific: SSRIs, SNRIs, lithium, valproate, beta-agonists and stimulants produce tremor through non-D2 mechanisms. Including it would label most antidepressants EPS-positive and blur the D2 anchor.
excluded.tardive dyskinesia: Delayed, cumulative syndrome not measured in 3-8 week placebo tables.
excluded.dyskinesia: In dopaminergic (levodopa, dopamine agonist) labels dyskinesia is a D2 AGONIST effect, the opposite mechanism.
excluded.restlessness: Not specific to akathisia; also anxiety/activation from serotonergic drugs.

excluded.fatigue: Non-specific (also asthenia, depression symptom); not an H1 readout.

excluded.increased appetite: Upstream of weight gain but a different measured endpoint; kept out so that the label means measured weight change reported as an adverse reaction.
excluded.weight tables (>=7% gain): Many labels report categorical weight gain in a separate Warnings table, not the adverse-reaction table. Those tables are not read here (different denominator and definition); only the adverse-reaction row counts.

excluded.mydriasis, tachycardia: Rarely tabulated; tachycardia has many non-muscarinic causes.

anticholinergic.notes: amblyopia and vision abnormal are included because pre-MedDRA COSTART labels (paroxetine, older TCAs) code blurred vision that way. Dry mouth and constipation also arise from alpha2 and noradrenergic mechanisms; the label is an anticholinergic-burden PHENOTYPE, not proof of muscarinic block. Terms combine by max.

excluded.dizziness: Vestibular/CNS dizziness is reported by almost every CNS drug; only the postural form is alpha1-specific.
excluded.hypotension: Non-postural; includes vasodilator and volume effects.

cell_values.number: A cell that is a plain number, optionally followed by '%', is that percentage.
cell_values.n_and_pct: A cell 'a (b)' or 'a (b%)' is count a with percentage b when the column or table header says n (%) or the parenthetical carries a % sign; 'a% (b)' is percentage a. Otherwise the cell is recorded as unparsed and not used.
cell_values.less_than: '<1' (or '< 0.5' etc.) is recorded verbatim as censored; for arithmetic it takes half the bound (0.5 for '<1') and the arm carries censored=true. A binary label that depends on a censored value is still computed but flagged.
cell_values.dash_or_blank: '-', en dash, em dash, '0' or blank in a row that has a value in another arm is 0, flagged dash_as_zero (labels use a dash for 'no cases' or 'below reporting threshold').
cell_values.footnotes: Footnote symbols (*, dagger, letters in <sup>) are stripped before parsing.

tables.placebo_controlled: An adverse-reaction table is placebo-controlled when at least one column header (after rowspan/colspan expansion and concatenation of header rows) contains 'placebo' and that column holds numeric cells.
tables.drug_columns: Non-placebo numeric columns. If any column header names the drug (INN or brand name from openfda), only those columns are drug arms (active comparators such as haloperidol in a risperidone table are excluded). If no column header names any drug, every non-placebo numeric column is a drug arm and the table is flagged drug_column_unnamed. Columns whose header says 'all doses', 'total', 'pooled' or 'combined' are a pooled drug column.
tables.n_per_arm: Read only from the column header cell (N=, n=, n =), never from prose.
tables.threshold: The inclusion threshold sentence is recorded verbatim from the table caption or, failing that, the last sentence of the adverse_reactions prose that mentions the table and a percent sign. It is NOT parsed into a number (project rule: no number regexed out of prose).
tables.population: Caption text, verbatim, is the population/indication.
tables.primary_table_rule: Among a label's placebo-controlled tables: (1) exclude tables whose caption mentions pediatric, paediatric, children, adolescent or child if any adult/unspecified table exists; (2) prefer monotherapy over captions mentioning adjunct/adjunctive/add-on/combination; (3) largest total stated n (drug arms + placebo); tables with no stated n rank after tables with n; (4) first in label order. One primary table per drug, used for all five liabilities; all other placebo-controlled tables are recorded under 'other_tables' with their own values.

label_selection.order: Labels in drugs.json order (NDA holder first, then by effective_time).
label_selection.single_ingredient: Labels whose openfda.substance_name lists more than one substance, or whose generic_name contains ' and ' or '/', are used only when no single-ingredient label qualifies.
label_selection.systemic_route: Labels whose route is only OPHTHALMIC, TOPICAL, NASAL, OTIC, CUTANEOUS, VAGINAL, RECTAL (local), DENTAL or INTRAVITREAL are used only when no systemic-route label qualifies.
label_selection.priority: First qualifying label that has at least one placebo-controlled adverse-reaction table; failing that, the first label with any adverse-reaction table (absolute fallback); failing that, the first label with adverse-reaction prose (absolute fallback, listed-in-prose only); failing that, absent.

pooling.rule: If the primary table has a pooled drug column ('all doses', 'total', 'pooled', 'combined'), its value is the pooled drug %. Otherwise pooled drug % is the n-weighted mean of the dose arms when every arm states n, else the unweighted mean of the arms. The pooled risk difference is pooled drug % minus placebo %. Per-arm risk differences are also recorded, and max_arm_rd is the largest of them.
pooling.multiple_placebo_columns: If a table has more than one placebo column, they are pooled by the same rule.

binary_rule.placebo_subtracted: positive (1) iff pooled risk difference >= 5 percentage points AND pooled drug % >= 2 x placebo %. negative (0) otherwise.
binary_rule.justification: This is the FDA labeling convention for 'commonly observed, drug-related' adverse reactions (incidence >= 5% and at least twice placebo; FDA guidance 'Adverse Reactions Section of Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products - Content and Format' (2006), and common in PLR labels as 'incidence >= 5% and at least twice that for placebo'), tightened from an absolute 5% floor to a 5-point risk difference so that a common background event (constipation 8% vs placebo 4%) does not pass on the ratio alone. Both conditions must hold: the difference guards against tiny absolute rates with large ratios (2% vs 0.5%), the ratio guards against noisy differences on high-background terms (dry mouth 25% vs 19%).
binary_rule.absent_below_threshold: A liability none of whose terms appears in the primary placebo-controlled table is negative (0) with drug_pct and placebo_pct null and flag absent_below_threshold. Justification: label tables list reactions above a stated incidence threshold (usually >=1-5% and more than placebo), so absence implies drug incidence below that threshold or not above placebo; under either the 5-point rule cannot be met when the threshold is <=5%. The verbatim threshold sentence is recorded so a reader can check it.
binary_rule.absolute_fallback: When the selected label has no placebo-controlled table: positive (1) iff a mapped term has drug % >= 10 (CIOMS 'very common') in a non-placebo adverse-reaction table; 0 if the table is present and the mapped terms are absent or below 10; null when only prose is available (recorded as listed_in_prose true/false, no number). Every such row carries basis 'absolute_fallback' and flagged true.
binary_rule.absent: No usable label or no adverse-reaction section: label null, basis 'absent'.

heldout: No held-out field is stored. Consumers apply pipeline.guards.v2_heldout(inn).

amendments.made_after_seeing: mirtazapine's primary table came out as 'Table 2: Adverse Reactions Leading to Discontinuation'
amendments.rule: Tables whose caption (including a title row inside the table) contains 'discontinu' are excluded: they report discontinuation, not incidence.
amendments.affects: table eligibility only; term map and margin unchanged

amendments.made_after_seeing: mirtazapine Tables 3 and 4 tie on n; label order picked the '>=5% and twice placebo' subset table
amendments.rule: primary_table_rule step (3): ties on total n are broken by the larger number of data rows, then label order.
amendments.affects: primary-table choice only; term map and margin unchanged

amendments.made_after_seeing: a scan of unmatched row labels containing liability words (no outcome values inspected for it): 'weight increase' x7, 'dystonic event(s)' x7, 'extrapyramidal event', 'any/other extrapyramidal event', 'akathisia events', 'vision abnormality', 'drowsy'
amendments.rule: Row labels (not the term map) are normalised before matching: a leading 'any'/'other'/'all' is dropped; singular 'event' -> 'events'; 'increase' -> 'increased'; 'abnormality/ies' -> 'abnormal'; 'dystonic event(s)' -> 'dystonia'; '<akathisia|parkinsonism|dystonia> event(s)' -> the bare term; 'drowsy'/'daytime drowsiness' -> 'drowsiness'. A row starting 'other' is never treated as the grouped row, so it is combined by max with the named sub-terms.
amendments.affects: row matching only; the term list, margin and pooling are unchanged

amendments.made_after_seeing: fluoxetine/clomipramine/trazodone tables place several trials side by side (MDD | OCD | bulimia; adults | children; inpatients | outpatients), each with its own placebo column, and the first build pooled the placebo arms across populations
amendments.rule: A table whose header has a spanning row splitting the arms into >=2 groups that each contain a placebo and a drug column is treated as one sub-table per group (table_index + column_group); each drug arm is compared only with its own group's placebo. The primary-table rule then runs over the sub-tables, with the group label appended to the caption so the adult and monotherapy steps see it.

amendments.made_after_seeing: lurasidone Table 20: arm headers span two body columns, which created duplicate arms; and the 'All LATUDA' column was pooled as if it were a dose arm
amendments.rule: A column whose last header cell is a colspan copy is not a separate arm. A header containing 'all ' (e.g. 'All LATUDA') is a pooled column, like 'total'/'all doses', and is excluded from dose arms.

amendments.made_after_seeing: spot-check: pimozide's placebo-controlled table (N=20 per arm) reports patient counts, which the first build read as percentages (dry mouth 5 vs 1 read as 5% vs 1%; it is 25% vs 5%)
amendments.rule: A table is a count table when nothing marks its values as percentages ('%', 'percent', 'incidence', 'rate' absent from caption and headers; no '%' or decimal in any value cell), every arm column states its N, every value is an integer no larger than its column's N, and at least one value is impossible as a rounded percentage of that N (no k <= N has round(100k/N) equal to it; e.g. 14 with N=20). The last condition was added after the first version also caught topiramate Table 6 (N=183/291), whose integer values are percentages. Its cells are converted to 100*count/N and the entry is flagged counts_converted.
amendments.affects: cell values of count tables only

amendments.made_after_seeing: an audit of the first build: phenol scored from an Anzemet (dolasetron) label and capsaicin from a diclofenac-with-capsaicin kit (universe name matching, fixed in scripts/v2_universe.py); ~25 drugs scored from local-route labels (eye drops, local anaesthetic infiltration, inhaled bronchodilators, antihistamine nasal spray) and some from multi-ingredient labels via fallback tiers; aripiprazole scored from its long-acting injectable label; olanzapine weight gain negative because weight is reported outside the adverse-reaction tables
amendments.rule: (1) Multi-ingredient and local-route labels are never used; local routes add infiltration, epidural, perineural, submucosal, percutaneous, intradermal, intracavernous, intra-articular; nasal, inhaled and rectal labels are local unless the drug has an ATC N code. (2) Among eligible labels, oral labels are tried first. (3) weight_gain labels are withheld (label null, flag label_withheld_A7); extracted numbers are kept.
amendments.affects: label eligibility and order, and the weight_gain label; term map and margin rule unchanged
